# rust-dashcore, vendored for evolite (FEAT-0037)

**Source:** [dashpay/rust-dashcore](https://github.com/dashpay/rust-dashcore) at `0dcdd823` ("feat(dash-spv)!: validate header difficulty against Dark Gravity Wave", #1161).

**Why:** this commit is the one that checks header difficulty against Dark Gravity Wave. Before it, past the last checkpoint, a peer could serve a chain of minimal difficulty. That matters on mainnet. Platform 575d961, which evolite builds on, still pins `aca0202`. Our root `Cargo.toml` uses `[patch."https://github.com/dashpay/rust-dashcore"]` to point all 12 crates, ours and Platform's, at this copy.

## What is here

- The root `Cargo.toml`, with `members` cut down to the 12 crates below, so cargo can read the workspace. Our root `Cargo.toml` excludes `vendor/rust-dashcore`.
- `LICENSE`.
- The crates `dash`, `crypto`, `hashes`, `internals`, `dash-network`, `dash-network-seeds`, `dash-spv`, `key-wallet`, `key-wallet-manager`, `git-state`, `rpc-client` and `rpc-json`.

## What was removed

- `.git`.
- Every crate's `tests/` folder and `dash/artifacts/`. Their data is read only by rust-dashcore's own tests: `include_bytes!` and `include_str!` under `#[cfg(test)]` or the `test-utils` feature, which evolite does not enable. We don't run those tests.
- The crates `fuzz`, `dash-spv-ffi`, `key-wallet-ffi`, `ffi-c-tests`, `rpc-integration-test`, `dash-spv-bench` and `masternode-seeds-fetcher`.
- Files at the root other than `Cargo.toml` and `LICENSE`.

`benches/` and `examples/` stay: the crates' manifests declare them, and cargo reads the declarations.

## What was changed

**One shim**, kept as its own file: [`evolite-shim.patch`](evolite-shim.patch). It is `git diff 0dcdd823` of `dash-spv/src/chain/checkpoints.rs`, and it only adds:

- `Checkpoint::height` becomes `pub`;
- `CheckpointManager::last_checkpoint()` returns the highest checkpoint, as in `aca0202`.

platform-wallet 575d961 (`wallet_lifecycle.rs`) still calls both. rust-dashcore #375 removed them. The birth height logic is unchanged: by default the header tip, otherwise the last checkpoint.

To check that the copy matches the source plus the shim, apply `evolite-shim.patch` to a clean `0dcdd823` checkout. The 12 crates' source must then be identical.

## When to remove it

When Platform ships with rust-dashcore ≥ `0dcdd823` (v5.1.0), remove this folder, the `[patch]` section and the `exclude` from our root `Cargo.toml`.

## evolite's own: fork handling (SPV item 1, plan 2026-11-14 §1)

Applied after the four above. `git diff evolite/spv-p0-final` in a clone of our own, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-fork`, branch `evolite/spv-fork-work` (`C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore` belongs to another session).

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-fork.patch` | — (**evolite, not from upstream**) | A valid branch was followed, and our chain trimmed, as soon as it branched off below the tip, whatever its work. A peer could make us drop blocks with one cheap header. | **Work decides:** a fork is followed (`ForkDetected`, then the trim and resync) only when its headers have strictly more proof of work (`ChainWork`) than our stored chain from the fork point to the tip. On equal work we stay on the chain seen first, as Dash Core does. **Held until then:** the branch stays in memory (`BlockHeadersManager::fork`), nothing trimmed, and its peer is asked for what follows (`getheaders` from the branch's tip). Headers that continue it are validated against stored ancestors plus the branch (continuity, PoW, DGW), then added and weighed again. At most `MAX_FORK_HEADERS` = 2016: beyond that the branch is dropped and its peer disconnected (`NetworkRequest::DisconnectPeer`, no ban: its headers were valid). **Final blocks:** the checkpoint and ChainLock rule is checked again when weighing, so a ChainLock that came since drops the branch. **The ban:** a peer whose fork headers fail validation, first or continuing, is disconnected and banned for an hour (`ChangeReason::InvalidHeaders`, `ban_duration`); a manual ban keeps its day. **Tests:** bad PoW and easier difficulty refused with the peer banned, first headers and continuing a held branch (AC-T1.1, 1.2; the mainnet DGW case of `evolite-fork-ban.patch` stays); less or equal work held, not followed, the peer asked for more (1.3); more work followed in one message or grown over several, and work rather than length decides (1.4); a ChainLock arriving under a held branch drops it, the existing checkpoint and ChainLock cases stay (1.5); too long without more work, dropped and disconnected; the hour's ban. Eight mutations, each red. **SPV item 1б (in the same patch): after a block race we noticed nothing.** If we stored N₁ while the network went on N₂ → N+1, every announcement had a parent we didn't have and was dropped, and the tip froze until a restart. Now, synced: headers that extend nothing we store, and a ChainLock (`CLSig`) for a block we don't store, send `getheaders` with a **block locator** as Dash Core builds one (the tip, the nine before it, then steps doubling back, the lowest stored header last). For a ChainLock it goes to the peer that sent it and one other. At most once per peer per `LOCATOR_ASK_INTERVAL` (30 s). The peer answers from our common ancestor, and the branch is weighed as above. The tip segment's fallback getheaders (stale `inv` announcements, a peer ahead of us, a resumed sync, announcements during sync) carried the tip's hash alone, which a peer on another branch answers from genesis; it now carries the locator too (`reset_tip_with_locator`). Our part's work is kept in the held branch until our tip moves (review note). **Tests:** the locator's shape; a block race asked for and followed (AC-T1б.1); a ChainLock for an unknown block, our own, and while syncing (1б.2); a stream of unconnecting announcements asks each peer once per interval (1б.3); the fallback carries the locator; our work read again when the tip moves. Eight more mutations, each red. | When upstream compares chain work before following a fork. |

## evolite's own: peers over subnets (SPV item 2b, plan 2026-11-14 §2б)

Applied after `evolite-fork.patch` (items 1 and 1б): `git diff evolite/spv-fork-locator` in our own clone, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-fork`, branch `evolite/spv-peers-on-1b`.

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-peers.patch` | — (**evolite, not from upstream**) | With our `max_peers` = 8 (evolite-chain's `client_config`; dash-spv's default is 3), one operator holding a block of addresses could still fill every connection and eclipse us. | **The subnet rule:** at most two outbound peers, connected or being connected, from one /16 (IPv4) or /32 (IPv6); an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address counts as IPv4 (`network::diversity`). **One gate:** `PeerPool::mark_connecting_within_subnets` checks and marks under one lock. Every outbound connect goes through `connect_to_peer` (known addresses, DNS fallback), which now says whether it started. The top-up loops count only connects that started, so a refused address leaves its place to the next. **Exempt:** peers the user configured (exclusive mode, «Own node»). **Tests:** five in one /16 give two (`pick_diverse`, AC-T2б.2), the pool's gate with a peer leaving, the manager's `connect_to_peer` in both modes. Six mutations, each red. | When upstream limits outbound peers per network group. |

## evolite's own: the stored masternode messages pruned (TECH-spv-prune, BUG-223)

Applied after `evolite-finalized-outputs.patch` (that one touches key-wallet only, this one dash-spv only: either order applies): `git diff evolite/spv-sml-peers` in a worktree of our own clone, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-prune`, branch `evolite/spv-prune` (commits `d028cf6d`, then review r1 `f3b476df` and `b62c79d0`). Design agreed with the architect, `docs/tasks/reviews/TECH-spv-prune-design.md`.

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-spv-prune.patch` | — (**evolite**; related draft `docs/upstream/BUG-79-dash-spv-masternode-replay-open-time.md`, not published) | Each start replays every stored MnListDiff and QRInfo, each checked against its coinbase. Nothing was ever deleted: each QRInfo is asked on a list the one before built, so the stored messages chain back to the first QRInfo from genesis. The start grew by about one message per 24 blocks (40 to 55 s on an older testnet copy). | **The cut:** more than `QRINFO_CUT_AT` = 8 stored QRInfos, the newest not from genesis already (`cut_due`: no second cut before the pruning ran), and the next is asked from genesis (no base), as a fresh storage asks. Once fed, the engine forgets the lists it didn't build (`cut_at_qr_info_from_genesis`), so no request after it takes a base from an older list. The work-block lists come back through the usual requests. **The pruning** (`PersistentMasternodeStorage::prune`, after a QRInfo is written): once a QRInfo from genesis is stored, only it and what is applied forward on its lists (or on genesis) can stay, ordered by bases, not height; everything from before the cut goes at once, older cuts included (review r1 M1). Of those, a list is needed when it lies in the engine's `retention_window` below the newest list, or when a kept message is applied on it. Each needed list is kept through the newest message that builds it, and so are that message's bases. Everything else goes, the file before its index entry. A file that doesn't read, or a block not in the header chain, stops the pruning. What remains is replayed and checked as before. **For the embedder:** `masternode_storage_stats()` gives `storage_ms`, `load_engine_ms`, `messages`, `pruned`, and the newest list's quorums verified and not, after the replay and after the first sync (evolite's journal `spv_start`, `mn_pruned`, `mn_quorums`). **Tests:** the window kept while a list in it still chains back; after the cut and the list asked again, the 12 before go, the reopened storage replays the same lists in the window, and the next diff applies; storing a QRInfo prunes once written; a missing file or an unknown block stops it; a QRInfo from genesis leaves only its lists to build on, while one on a list changes nothing; past 8 stored QRInfos the next is asked from genesis; a restart right after the cut keeps nothing from before it, the next base is one of the cut's lists, and no second cut is due; a stored cut asks no second one. Eight mutations, each red: height pruning, no closure over bases, judging an unknown block, no cut in the engine, no cut in the request, no cut in the pruning, a second cut while one waits, an older cut counted as applied on this one. `dash-spv` lib: 719 passed. **Lost:** `get_quorum_at_height`'s fallback that replays stored messages for a quorum the engine no longer holds can't reach before the cut. It served InstantSend locks of old transactions, which are final by ChainLock. | When upstream bounds the stored masternode messages. |

## evolite's own: only verified InstantLocks reach the wallet (BUG-111b)

Applied after `evolite-spv-prune.patch`: `git diff evolite/spv-prune` in a worktree of our own clone, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-islock`, branch `evolite/spv-islock-validated` (commit `955caf84`). Design agreed with the architect; its conditions are in `docs/tasks/reviews/BUG-111-r1.md`.

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-instantlock-validated.patch` | — (**evolite**; upstream only as a draft note, published with the customer's consent) | The InstantSend manager sends an InstantLock it could not verify yet (its cycle's quorum not known, or its signature failing) as `InstantLockReceived { validated: false }`, keeps it pending, and sends it again `validated: true` once it verifies; an expired one, or one whose signature still fails, is dropped. The mempool applied both. The wallet marked the transaction InstantSend, and platform-wallet's asset lock proof (identity creation, top-up, the pool from Core) took that lock from the record's context. The change of such a parent was trusted too. | **In `sync/mempool/sync_manager.rs`:** `InstantLockReceived { validated: true }` → `process_instant_send` as before; `validated: false` → nothing: no mark, no remembered lock for a transaction still to come, no wallet event. A genuine lock is only delayed until its quorum is known. **Tests:** unverified, then the same lock verified (the mempool entry, the wallet's record and its event); unverified before its transaction, the transaction then arrives unlocked; a lock that never verifies never locks the transaction, in two halves (the InstantSend manager never sends it verified: kept while its signature fails, dropped when expired; the mempool applies nothing however often it comes unverified). The mutant without the check fails the three mempool tests. `dash-spv` lib: 723 passed (1 ignored). | When upstream applies only verified InstantLocks. |

## evolite's own: wait for peers by how fast they answer (TECH-spv-peers)

Applied after `evolite-instantlock-validated.patch`: `git diff 955caf84` in a worktree of our own clone, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-peers`, branch `evolite/spv-fast-peers` (commits `91016c53`, then r1 `5e4034ca`). Measured in `docs/analysis/spv-headers-measure-2026-11-21.md`: on the first mainnet sync, header replies took 5.8 s at the median and 20.6 s at p90, 1 request in 8 timed out, and each lost one held the in-order write for 30 s.

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-fast-peers.patch` | — (**evolite**; nothing goes upstream without the customer) | The first mainnet sync was limited by slow and silent peers, not the CPU: a header segment waited a fixed 30 s for a lost reply while the others sat buffered (a 5-minute stall in the customer's run), QRInfo waited 10, 30, then 60 s, routing kept peers up to 4× slower than the best, and seeds that never answered were tried again. | **Adaptive timeouts** (`sync/download_coordinator.rs`: `AdaptiveTimeout`, `ReplyTimes`): header segments (shared by all segments of the pipeline) and MnListDiffs time a request at 3× the median reply, within 6..=15 s (15 s until five replies), a timeout counting with its wait; the 6 s floor is above `REQUEST_OWED_TIMEOUT`, so the retry goes to another peer. **The ceiling is not a wall (r1):** three timeouts in a row double it, up to 60 s, and it comes down a step with each answer within the base ceiling (an answer slower than that keeps it), so a network where every peer is slower than 15 s still syncs. **QRInfo:** first attempt 10 s, each retry (round robin, the next peer) 3× the median QRInfo reply within 10..=20 s (15 s while none is known), four attempts; timeouts are counted too, and two in a row double the 20 s, up to 60 s (r1): with peers that all take 35 s the third attempt waits 40 s and gets the list. **Routing** keeps peers within 2× of the best (`SLOW_MULTIPLIER`, was 4). **A slow peer is replaced** (`evict_slowest_peer`): 4× the median of the connected peers' means and over 3 s, with a replacement known, under the stuck-peer eviction's guards and cooldown. **Failed addresses** (`FailedPeers`) are skipped for a while, logged once: 15 min after a failed handshake, 5 min when it did not connect at all (it may be our network); with no peer connected, every failed address is tried again (r1: a start without a network, an outage). Verification is unchanged: proof of work, checkpoints, quorum signatures, the coinbase proofs. **Tests:** the adaptive timeout (median, bounds, too few, a timeout counted); answers and timeouts fed to the shared times; segments sharing them; the header retry's floor above the owed timeout; the QRInfo schedule; the 2× routing; the slow outlier (and none when alike, all fast or too few measured); a slow peer replaced only with a replacement; a failed address not tried while held; r1: peers that all answer headers in 20 s or QRInfo in 35 s still get through, and the ceiling comes back down; failed addresses come back after their time, and all at once with no peer connected. `dash-spv` lib: 734 passed (1 ignored). | When upstream times requests by its peers' replies, or the customer chooses another way. |

## evolite's own: the window a segment's headers are checked on (BUG-257)

Applied after `evolite-fast-peers.patch`: `git diff 5e4034ca` in a worktree of our own clone, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-bug257`, branch `evolite/bug257-dgw-window` (commit `955661f4`).

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-dgw-window.patch` | — (**evolite**; the bug is in our carrying over of #1304, `evolite-fork-validate.patch`) | Headers that follow a segment's tip were checked (`segment_ancestors`) on the checkpoint's headers put right under the segment's last 24 buffered ones, whatever lay between. After a drain (the in-order segment's buffer moves into the store) the window ended at the checkpoint: on testnet, 26 days before, so the «more than 2 hours» rule asked the proof-of-work limit (QA, testnet from zero: «Invalid difficulty at height 1266001: bits 0x1e01f982, required 0x1e0fffff»), and every honest peer that served the chain was banned. On mainnet a stale or mixed window gives a wrong Dark Gravity Wave the same way. | **The window ends at the parent:** a segment gives its last buffered headers (at most 24) and the height under them (`SegmentTail`); below them the store (after a drain), or the checkpoint's headers only while the buffer still reaches down to the checkpoint it starts at. Each part must join the next, and the whole must end at the batch's parent. **Nothing to check on** (the headers between neither buffered nor stored, a drain that never reached the store): the batch is neither checked nor taken, nobody is banned, and the pipeline starts again from the stored tip (a WARN line). A header never enters the chain without its difficulty checked. **Of two segments ending at one hash** (a finished one whose tip is the checkpoint the next one starts at): the one still downloading. **Tests**, on real testnet headers (1250001..1250010 and 1265950..1266010, from a synced store, in `src/sync/block_headers/`): the QA refusal reproduced on the checkpoint's window and the real chain passing on its own; a partly drained segment checked on its stored headers; a lost drain bans nobody and restarts from the stored tip; a forged header on a drained segment still refused and banned; a segment's first headers checked on its checkpoint; headers across a segment boundary checked on the next segment; the restart does not loop. `test_segment_tail` replaces `test_segment_ancestors`, which asserted the old gap. Four mutations, each red. | When upstream checks a segment's headers on a window ending at their parent. |

## evolite's own: the security audit of 2026-11-22 (four findings in the vendor copy)

Applied after `evolite-dgw-window.patch`, in this order, one commit per finding: in a worktree of our own clone, `C:\reps\deps\rust-dashcore-sec`, branch `evolite/sec-audit-r1` (on `955661f4`). Each patch is `git diff` against the one before: F2 `955661f4..2fec925a`, F6 `..af74cdd7`, F8 `..15991fd1`, F4 `..711c7e00`. The fixes come from the audit's patches (`CLAUDE-SECURITY-20261122-182802`), applied in evolite on `sec/audit-2026-11-22`; F8 with the architect's review r1 Should 1, F4 as the audit wrote it until BUG-283 (`docs/tasks/reviews/SEC-audit-2026-11-22-r1.md`). The clone's test run is `docs/tasks/checks/sec-audit-2026-11-22-vendor-tests.txt`.

| Patch | Upstream | Why | What it does | When to remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evolite-sec-f2-fork-needs-checked-headers.patch` | — (**evolite**; on our `evolite-fork.patch`) | **F2:** a batch whose first header's parent we don't store skips the validator (`Attach::Nowhere`), yet `fork_height` could still find a stored parent for the headers after its first one (a header we store, at the batch's start). The unchecked headers after it could then start a fork and win it with claimed work and no proof of work, and the chain and the wallet were trimmed. | **Only a validated batch (`Attach::At`) may start a fork:** for any other, `fork_height` is not asked. The batch is then handled as before for headers that extend nothing we store (synced: our locator to its peer). **Test** (`sync::block_headers::manager`): `an_unvalidated_batch_behind_a_stored_header_starts_no_fork`, where a stored header followed by a forged one with no proof of work and far more claimed work is not held, nothing is trimmed, nobody is banned, and its peer is asked with our locator. | With `evolite-fork.patch`, when upstream compares chain work before following a fork. |
| `evolite-sec-f6-announcements-bounded.patch` | — (**evolite**) | **F6:** a peer's block `inv` hashes went into `pending_announcements` with no limit, and nothing pruned them during the header sync. Every one kept the sync from completing (it asks for them first), so one peer could grow memory without bound and hold the sync back forever with hashes of blocks that don't exist. | **Bounded:** at most `MAX_PENDING_ANNOUNCEMENTS` = 500; the rest of an `inv` past it is dropped. **Not forever:** once the pipeline is complete, announced blocks are asked for, with our locator, for at most `PENDING_ANNOUNCEMENTS_SYNC_WAIT` = 20 s. Then the sync completes without them, with a WARN line. **Tests** (`sync::block_headers::manager`): `the_block_announcements_held_are_bounded`, `announcements_that_never_come_do_not_keep_the_sync_from_completing`, `an_announced_block_is_asked_for_until_it_arrives`. | When upstream bounds and expires the announcements held during sync. |
| `evolite-sec-f8-instantlock-cache-verified.patch` | — (**evolite**; on our `evolite-instantlock-validated.patch`) | **F8:** an InstantLock was cached under its txid whether or not it verified, and any later lock for that txid was dropped as a duplicate. Anyone can send a well-formed lock with a garbage signature first, and the genuine, quorum-signed lock was then never taken. | **Only a verified lock suppresses later ones** for its txid (`is_transaction_locked`). A lock identical to one already pending is skipped, so a re-sent lock does not fill the queue. **The cache:** a verified lock becomes the txid's entry; an unverified one is cached only while the txid has none, and never replaces another. The pending lock that verifies (here or in `validate_pending`) takes the entry, and a pending one whose txid is locked meanwhile is dropped: one verified lock, and one event, per txid. **At most 4 pending for one txid** (`MAX_PENDING_PER_TXID`, review r1 Should 1): forgeries for one txid would otherwise fill the 500 places and push out other txids' genuine locks. Past 4, a new lock for that txid is not queued and those waiting stay, so a forgery sent after the genuine lock cannot push it out. One sent before it can take a place; that txid then waits for its ChainLock. **Tests** (`sync::instantsend::manager`): `a_forged_lock_sent_first_does_not_shadow_the_genuine_one`, `the_pending_lock_that_verifies_is_the_one_cached`, `forged_locks_for_one_txid_take_a_few_places_only` (a mutation without the cap is red). | When upstream caches and deduplicates only verified InstantLocks. |
| `evolite-sec-f4-signers-within-members.patch` | — (**evolite**; on `evolite-mnlist-verify.patch`, upstream #1200) | **F4:** a rotated quorum's commitment counted the signer bits toward the threshold over its whole bit set, but the aggregate signature was checked only over the members rebuilt from the peer's snapshots. A peer could shrink the members, so signer bits past them counted with no key checked, and forged quorums were marked Verified, and so were the InstantLocks they "signed". | **As Dash Core's `CFinalCommitment::Verify`** (`sml_engine::validation::validate_signed_by`): a signer bit or a valid-member bit past the members is refused (`SignerBeyondMembers`, `ValidMemberBeyondMembers`). **A masternode signs once,** keyed by its ProRegTx hash as Dash Core keys members: rebuilt members that name one masternode at several indexes and sign there are refused (`DuplicateSigner`). **The threshold is counted over the members** (`InsufficientSigners`), then the aggregate check as before. The three new errors are in `dash/src/sml/quorum_validation_error.rs`. **`DuplicateSigner` is temporary** (review r1 and its addendum): Dash Core has no such rule, and repeats are normal when there are fewer masternodes than places (LLMQ_60_75: 1920 places, testnet a few hundred masternodes), so it may refuse genuine testnet quorums. Without it, one masternode key repeated in swapped snapshots would pass. It goes in one vendor delivery with BUG-283, which checks QRInfo's `last_commitment_per_index` against the tip list's quorums already verified against the coinbase. Until then a live testnet InstantSend shows whether genuine cycles stay Verified. **Tests** (`sml_engine::validation`): `signer_bits_past_the_members_are_refused`, `valid_member_bits_past_the_members_are_refused`, `signers_among_the_members_must_reach_the_threshold`, `a_masternode_signing_at_more_than_one_index_is_refused`, and `fewer_members_than_the_size_with_clear_bits_past_them_reach_the_signature_check` (an honest short member set still reaches the signature check). The whole `sml_engine` set passes, the real mainnet QRInfo included. | When upstream checks a rotated commitment's bits against its members as Dash Core does. |

- `dashcore`: `merkle_tree::block`, `sml::masternode_list` and `network::message_sml`, 29 passed.

**Not ported, needs #902:** upstream's own assertions on the #902 mock network (`MockNetworkManager::banned_peers`) and the `release_request` of the answered locator; their meaning is covered by the tests above.

**Copy = source + patches.** A clean `0dcdd823` with `evolite-shim.patch`, `evolite-mnlist-verify.patch`, `evolite-fork-validate.patch`, `evolite-fork-ban.patch`, `evolite-fork.patch`, `evolite-peers.patch`, `evolite-sml-peers.patch`, `evolite-finalized-outputs.patch`, `evolite-spv-prune.patch`, `evolite-instantlock-validated.patch`, `evolite-fast-peers.patch`, `evolite-dgw-window.patch`, `evolite-sec-f2-fork-needs-checked-headers.patch`, `evolite-sec-f6-announcements-bounded.patch`, `evolite-sec-f8-instantlock-cache-verified.patch` and `evolite-sec-f4-signers-within-members.patch` applied in this order gives the 12 crates here, `tests/` and `artifacts/` aside.
